utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karnavas, are you ready for the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour. Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And are there any protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We will be asking face distortion and just a pseudonym for this particular witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Any objections? Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: None, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Your request is granted. Since we are in this small courtroom, so there won't be any visitors in the public gallery. So we'll have the face distortion, and we do not put the shade around this witness. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's fine with me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down, please. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. Examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could please show you what has been marked as Exhibit D125 for identification purposes. Please look at it and see if that is your name. Is that your name, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes, it is my name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could go into private session so we can discuss the gentleman's background, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you recall about what day that order came? Assuming that Srebrenica fell on the 11th and people were being evacuated as of the 12th of July, using that as a framework, could you tell us, if you recall, what day you received that order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: The day before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did it take you to muster up and report to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: About two or three hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so do you have a recollection as to what time you got into Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Well, not precisely, but sometime in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if Bratunac -- I mean, if Srebrenica fell on the 11th, what day would you have gotten into Bratunac, to your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: The 10th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And when you got to Bratunac, were you able to meet with Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall where it was that you met him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I think it was near the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, was the company given any particular orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Not at that moment; a little later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told how long you would be there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told where you would be staying overnight, in the event you stayed overnight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Nothing. They didn't tell us any of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever asked to go to the Bratunac Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever go to the Bratunac Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever introduced to any of the officers from the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever told whether you would be receiving orders from the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Not to me they didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you recall, what was the first order that the 1st Company received from Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: The first order was that I should get up close to Zuti Most, I think it was called, that I should take shelter there and wait for further orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes, I did, towards evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. How did you get to the Zuti Most, if you recall? If you don't recall, that's okay, just tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I think I went on foot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And when you got there do you recall about what time it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: It was already getting dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you do -- did you have any -- other than your order to go there, were you instructed to engage in any other activities at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether your company engaged in any activities at that point, when you got there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, it didn't. The men were just sitting around in a ditch by the road and resting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us approximately how long you were in that location.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I stayed there the whole night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall whether there was any action or any engagement with anybody during that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Not there, but I did hear detonations coming from the direction of Srebrenica and the hills up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So you could hear some action, but your men -- you and the men were not engaged. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the next day, if you recall, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: On the next day I think the sun was already up. We set out in the direction of Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And how far did you get?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go all the way to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes. We went to Potocari, but not all in one go. We kept coming back to our starting position; I don't know why. I don't know what was going on there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall receiving any orders to go to Potocari, and if so, by whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I think Mr. Borovcanin ordered us to set out toward Potocari along that road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did -- was this communicated in person, or was it communicated by some other means?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what happened after that, do you know? Could you please tell us. You said you were going towards Potocari and coming back, but could you tell us what eventually happened on that day, if you recall.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't remember. There were already some people there before me, army, police, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, is this the same day, just so we understand, is this the same day when the evacuation takes place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I think it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So then we're talking about the 12th and not the 11th. When you get to Potocari, do you recall about what time it would have been?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I can't be precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what you were able to observe.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I saw a large number of women, children, elderly all gathered around the UNPROFOR base.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do we -- do you recall what your specific orders were at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I understood that we were supposed to stand in front of those people and provide security for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right and why did they need security if the DutchBat were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't know. The DutchBat was to the left, to the side. And there was some sort of soldiers in front. I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I take it you were not able to recognise them, even by their insignia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. How long did you stay in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Not long. I don't know how long it was exactly. We sat to one side. There was some houses nearby. And as there was already a certain number of soldiers or policemen standing in front of those people, we stood to one side, to the right. In fact, we sat down next to those houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you receive any orders eventually while you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes. Soon I think General Ratko Mladic arrived with an escort and then Ljubisa Borovcanin came. I also saw Dusko Jevic from the special police. And it was then that I received an order that was transmitted to me by Ljubisa Borovcanin in person, that I should immediately return in the direction of Bratunac. I saw from a distance that he was having a vehement discussion with General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me stop you here. First of all, how close were you to General Mladic when he showed up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: About 150 or 200 metres. I can't be very precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to hear him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: As soon as he arrived in front of that mass of people, he addressed them and he told them that he was General Ratko Mladic, that they shouldn't be afraid, something to that effect, that they would be allowed to travel, that they should not be afraid of anything, that nobody would hurt them, something to that effect. He said this in a very loud voice so that I could hear it, too, even though I was so far away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And up until this time, you still had not received any particular orders while you were in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall if there were any buses there at that point in time when you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you said that Mr. Borovcanin at some point in time gave you some orders. Could you please tell us to the best of your recollection what those orders were and what the exchange was between you and Mr. Borovcanin, the conversation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: He told me that General Mladic had ordered him to have police forces leave Potocari immediately, that they should go to Bratunac and then Zvornik, because most of the Muslim combatants had broken through the line and were moving in the direction of Zvornik, that they had set some vehicles on fire along the way, something like that. That these forces should be prevented from entering Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, this is what Mr. Borovcanin told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he told me at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did he tell you about his exchange with Mladic, with General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I think there were certain problems between the two of them, that General Mladic literally drove him away from that place, saying: "What is the police doing here? Why don't they go where there are problems?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, after Mr. Borovcanin gave you -- well, let me back up. Did Mr. Borovcanin give you any specific orders of where to go from there and to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: We went off in the direction of Bratunac, and there we waited for new instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall -- when you had left Potocari towards Bratunac, had the buses arrived by then, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I think the first buses had started arriving when I got to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you got to Bratunac, for how -- where did you go to wait for your next set of instructions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: We were near the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about how long were you there before you received instructions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't remember precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, do you remember what instructions you eventually received?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes. Ljubisa Borovcanin arrived and said that we should go towards Zvornik, because communication had been cut off at a certain point and that it was necessary to ensure the normal flow of traffic because soon the buses would start moving, which were to transport those people gathered there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, towards Zvornik, that's a pretty vague description. Did he tell you any particular area where you had to situate yourself at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't remember precisely, but I do know he said: "Go in the direction of Konjevic Polje and there you'll see, there are some soldiers and policemen along the road." We were to link up with them and stay there in order to secure that communication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did he ever tell you to whom -- whether you had to report to anybody once you got there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well -- and I take it that eventually you and the others went to that area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: We set off in the direction of Konjevic Polje, and when we got close to a place which I think is called Sandici along the road we saw people lying down behind little shelters, because there was shooting from the direction of Bratunac toward Konjevic Polje, along the left side of the road, shooting from infantry weapons, all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And so where did you eventually end up at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I deployed my unit near a large house in Sandici. There was a downwards slope. I know that you go down from a hill into a valley, and there we took shelter behind sheltering screens along the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any particular reason why you chose that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Up to that large house, there were already policemen and soldiers lined up. And in that area, there was a lot of firing from infantry weapons, from the hilltops on the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, when you got there, since you had to sort of link up, did you meet with anybody to introduce yourself and the rest of the men that were there with you so at least they would know who their neighbor was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I saw that members of the special brigade of the police were there already. We linked up -- or rather, we simply got in connection with the last people in that line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And which special brigade are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: The Sekovic platoon of the special brigade of the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you know who was commanding them at the time, at that moment, at that location, on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I didn't see the man nor do I know him, but I heard from those people. I don't even know his name. This is the man they called "the Officer," that was his nickname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us about what time of day it would have been when you got to that location by Sandici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I think it was towards evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And is that because you are using the sunlight as a basis of determining what time it was, or did you have some other means, like looking at a watch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't have a watch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please tell us what was going on when you arrived there. What was it like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: As I said, there was a constant exchange of fire on both sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well -- and what were you and the men doing of the 1st Company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: We lay there behind those barriers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you go into the terrain to try to search for and capture or kill the enemy forces that were firing upon you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No. It was very difficult to raise your head behind those barriers or shelters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you at that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: We stayed there the whole night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the next day? Now we're talking the 13th of July. Do you recall what happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Just before dawn, day was beginning to break. There was again a large attack. One policeman was killed and three were severely wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And were they your men, the men that were in that --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: They were members of my company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me show you what has been marked as D126 for identification purposes. If we could look at this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And perhaps, Your Honour, we could go into a private session, since we'll be discussing some names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once the -- one of the men was killed, do you recall what you did after this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I think we organised for them to be transported and given assistance towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you remain there or did you go anywhere as a result of this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: When it got light I went toward Bratunac to visit the family of the policeman who had been killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And how long did you stay in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly, but it was two or three hours, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then from there -- once you were in Bratunac, did you make any reporting to anybody? Did you have to report to and give an accounting as to what had happened and what was going on in the field?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. After Bratunac, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I went back to the spot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it you had not moved from the spot that you had been located from -- that you and the other men had stationed yourselves the previous day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you have any idea about what time it would have been when you returned to where the other men were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't know precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us when you got there what was happening around that area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I saw that people were starting coming out of the woods on the left-hand side of the road from the hills, and they were crossing the road. There was already a group of some 10 or 15 men there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you say the left side of the road. So just so -- some of us haven't been there; hopefully we'll go there. But just so I'm clear, if you're heading towards Konjevic Polje, the left side -- you're talking about the left side of the road, if you are facing in that direction or towards Zvornik. Correct? So Bratunac would be behind you, Konjevic Polje is in front of you, and you're talking about that left side of the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes, yes. When you're moving from the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, was there still -- was there fighting still going on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please describe to us what you were able to observe at that point in time, when you were stationed there by Sandici.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Some people were coming out carrying others who were wounded, others were yelling at them from the hills, even shooting at them. When those people came out, they cursed Zulfo Tursunovic and his men who were preventing them from coming out. The fighting would stop for a while, there would be a lull, and then it would start again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were you fighting back? Were you shooting back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes. The whole line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you order to any of your men to shoot at anyone who was surrendering?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No. People were coming down and those policemen were going there and even helping the people get out of the stream, because there was a flat piece of land there, low-lying land, and they were helping people get out, even carrying them. Nobody was shooting at those people. If you were there, you saw the slope on the left-hand side. And that's where most of the shooting was coming from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you recall when you were there capturing any prisoners or getting a hold of people that were surrendering?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I'm not quite clear on your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone surrender to you or to the men that were with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: They were passing by the people. It wasn't just one place, it was the house or several houses, three or four positions. So they would pass by and go across the road and across the meadow and that's the route they took.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But what I'm saying is did you come into possession of anyone who was surrendering himself to hold on to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, as I understand it, people were surrendering, were they not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes, they were coming out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what was happening to those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: They were going up to the meadow, which was behind our backs to the left, above us. And they sat there on the grass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So basically that's just across the road, is it not, on the right side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: About 100 to 150 metres from our positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The previous day, did anyone surrender, to your recollection, the first day you got there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, who told -- if you know, who told those individuals that were surrendering to go and stand or sit by the meadow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't know. I thought they -- I think they just did it of their own accord, or rather, all the people there said: Go up there and sit down. The police, the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they were being guarded by the police and the soldiers. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: They were in front of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, while they were -- do you recall about how many ended up in that area? How many men approximately surrendered themselves and placed themselves in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I couldn't really say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. While they were there, do you recall anyone coming over there and speaking with these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't know who exactly and at what time, but at one point, at that bend, General Mladic turned up with an escort of about ten soldiers of some kind. He went up to some 50 people perhaps and told them to sit. They got up. He said: "Sit. I'm General Ratko Mladic." And he was speaking very loudly so I could hear him. And then they started clapping. They clapped to him and said: "Long live Ratko Mladic." And he said to them -- perhaps I'm not going to be very exact when I quote. But the gist of it is: "The Muslim soldiers, at this point in time, your families, your brothers, sisters, mothers, are passing by in buses and going in the desired direction where they want to go and you'll be doing the same. You'll be going away. You're going to be brought some bread and water now, and you're going to leave this place and follow them, except for those who have Serbian blood and civilian blood on their hands, and they will be tried."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: They started clapping again. He went down to the road, and I don't know whether he went to Konjevic Polje or what direction he took after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did the general by any chance stop to talk to you or anyone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to those men, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Some of them went off in the buses, and others went off on foot in the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who ordered them to leave that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Believe me when I say I don't know. Some buses arrived, so some went in the buses; others were escorted by the soldiers or policemen. And they went off in the direction of Bratunac, some on foot and some in the buses, as I've already said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And those soldiers or policemen that were escorting them, did you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask them where they were from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Well, this is how it was: It was a beehive. There were so many people. People were inquisitive, so they came in to see what was happening from Bratunac. Other would be passing by. There would be comings and goings. They would see people they recognised, neighbours or whoever. So it was a general commotion. And then suddenly the buses turned up and they would go off with those people there. Now, what time it was, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you at any point in time make any inquiries as to where they were going and who was it that was taking them? On whose orders were they being escorted away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I didn't wonder about that, because I wasn't in charge of the people up there. I assumed somebody knew what was to be done with them from the command, the soldiers, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, before getting there or while you were there, were you ever given any specific instructions as to what you should do to anyone that you had captured or surrendered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't think anybody knew that when they were there. It was a very confused state, and I think there was general surprise when the people started coming up on to the road. Nobody knew what was actually happening, that's how I understood it at least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever ask -- did you or the men that were there with you ever call out asking the Muslims that were in the column to come down and surrender?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Well, I did hear some young guys by the house up there, that they used a megaphone, a loudspeaker, and were calling out to them: "Come down towards the house," and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And were these young guys, as you put it, by the house up there, were they with you? Were they part of that group that you were with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No. I didn't know some of those people, and others I think belonged to the special police brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm about to get into a segment that may take a little while to describe, so if we could break five minutes early.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I think we'll resume at 20 minutes to 11.00. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, while you were situated in that area on the 13th of July and these folks were surrendering themselves in that area by Sandici where you were located, did you ever come across two young individuals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Can you be more precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you ever come across two young boys that were among the crowd or they were coming down or surrendering themselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes. They weren't in the mass of people, in the crowd. These two young boys had come from the grass, the long grass. It's difficult for me to explain the area. They were very young boys.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And could you please describe to us what happened to the young boys.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I went up to them when they crossed the barrier. I asked them where they were from and how they came to be there. They were crying. Their clothes were all torn. They were dirty. And one of them said that he had followed his father, but that his father had gone off somewhere and he didn't know where his mother was either. At first, I didn't know what to do with them. And the buses were going past at that point, carrying the women, children, and the elderly men. And I turned to the first bus that came up, I stopped it. And as it happened, I knew the driver who was driving the bus. So I called out to the man -- or rather, I called out to a man I knew from before while I was working at the traffic policeman. He was a Bosniak, a Muslim, that is to say, who was sitting in front, the co-driver's seat, in fact. He was sitting in the bus next to the driver. I said hello to him and told him to move up a bit, to move to the back of the bus and to take in the two children because I didn't know what to do with them, who to hand them over to, who to entrust them to. So they got on to the bus and sat there right next to the driver. I told the driver to see what he can do -- could do and hand them over to somebody, whether he -- to ask around whether anybody knew who the parents were and where they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us why you told the individual who was sitting up front to sit in the back of the bus.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Well, not right to the back, just to move from the front seat, to make room for the children because the bus was packed with the passengers. So I just said to him: "Move over. Go back a bit" - I know him well, so I could say that to him - "and leave room for the children."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could go into private session just for a few moments, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecution on 14 October 2000. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this incident that we -- now is being verified by one of the Prosecutor's own witnesses was not mentioned by you at the time. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I didn't remember at that point in time. The investigator asked me whether I had seen anybody I knew, and I couldn't remember who I had actually seen at that particular moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I -- so that's the explanation as to why you didn't tell this to Mr. Ruez when he asked you whether you had recognised anyone on that road while you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes, I just couldn't remember at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you know what eventually happened to all those men that were taken away from Sandici? Do you know what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: They got into the buses and went off in the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time, do you know -- at the time, did you know where they were heading towards or what their final destination would be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I just thought: Well, they're going to Bratunac. They got on to the buses to be taken there. Because I heard General Mladic telling them that they would be exchanged, or I don't know what, and taken to Kladanj and Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Had anyone at that point in time told you that perhaps they were about to be executed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No. It never entered my mind. Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And incidentally, getting back to that bus incident where you put the children on, the individual that you recognised sitting in the front and you asked to step back, about how old was he at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Not more than 50.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you recognise any other men or did you see -- did you see, not recognise, but did you see any other men in the bus at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes, I did, several.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any reason why you did not ask that gentleman that you knew as well as the other men to step out of the bus and join the rest of those who had surrendered themselves in Sandici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No. The people were coming by on foot and the others were already sitting in the bus on their way to Kladanj and Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you at any point in time, sir, been given any instructions to stop buses and to check to see whether there were men of military age, say the range from 16 to 60, for you to take out and hold for --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, and believe me, we didn't pay attention to the buses going by either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when the men from Sandici left, did you keep an eye on them to see where eventually they went to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, I didn't have occasion to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sitting here today, do you know where they ended up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, there was an incident in Kravica at the Kravica agricultural warehouse. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, from where you were situated, where you and the men were situated, could you see the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: We were in a depression, and then there was an elevation. The road ascends to the top of the hill. And then you go in the direction of Kravica. It's about 2 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did -- after the men left, did there come a time when you heard a significant portion of firing as if there was a gun battle, fighting, going on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I have to repeat. The whole time while we were there, there would be a sudden lull and then there would be sporadic gunfire, both to the right of us and to the left of us. So if it was quiet all the time, you would be able to assess what side it was coming from. But as the situation was, it was very difficult to say, to assess that the shooting was coming from the left or from the right, for example.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So do you -- does anything stand out, though, in your mind that sometime during that day there was significant gunfire coming from a particular direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, I couldn't really say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us when was it that you learned about the incident at the Kravica agricultural warehouse.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: An hour or two later, perhaps more. People began to talk. Because people -- you must understand, people were coming and going all the time, passing by that way. And they were saying that an incident had taken place, that an officer was wounded, and I learnt that a policeman was dragged forcibly into the hangar and strangled, and that a rifle that he had in his hand was taken away, and that there was some shooting in which this officer was wounded. So that's how I came to learn of that, from the people that were passing by, they talked about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I want to go step by step now. Now, Officer, we're not talking about an officer, but someone with the nickname of "Officer." Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This individual who was called "Officer," do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, I don't know to the present day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it from your answer that you had never met him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, I never saw him. Perhaps I did see him, but I didn't know who he was, that that was the man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you know or did you learn at some point in time with which -- in which unit he was serving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I heard that he was the commander or chief of that Sekovici detachment, part of the special police brigade, the Sekovici Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to the best of your recollection, you did not meet with that individual prior to this incident in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the police officer who was killed, did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I don't know what the man's name was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what unit he was from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I heard that he was a member of the special police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Special police of the special brigade that we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes. The Sekovici Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you by any chance go to the Kravica agricultural warehouse to take a look for yourself to see what had happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a reason why you didn't go there, even out of curiosity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No. I heard about this incident two or three hours after it happened. I didn't feel any need to go up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. After the men left from Sandici, what did you and the other men that were with you doing? They left, they went to Sandici. And from Sandici, they left for the Kravica warehouse. What did you and the men that you were with, what did you do? Did you stay there? Did you relocate yourselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, no. We stayed there until dusk, because people were still coming out of those woods up there on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, if they were still coming out of the woods, did you or the other men that you were with come across any of those men who were surrendering?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: They went out on to the field, gathered there, and at dusk buses were coming, some from one direction, others from another. I have no idea who they were transporting and where. And they got on to one of those buses and went off to Bratunac. It was already getting dark, and that's where I finished up on that part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you been given any particular orders as to what to do with any of those men? We're talking about now the second shift?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No. No, nothing. They just got on to the bus and left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who ordered those buses to come there to pick up these men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was operating the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether those buses had soldiers on them or military police, or police? MUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: You mean as an escort?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. As an escort or as security.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I couldn't say who was inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that particular day, the 13th of July, did you by any chance see Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I think I did see him at one point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did he -- do you recall now, do you recall whether you and the men received any particular orders from Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Nothing. He said when this is finished, he was referring to the escort of the buses, we were free to leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you see anyone from the 2nd Company? You were with the 1st, right? Now I'm talking about the 2nd Company.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: It's hard to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: People were passing by, coming and going all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the 2nd Company was assigned to any tasks in that area when you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know at that time who the commander was of the 2nd Company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Slavoljub Mladjenovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, I knew him. He was the komandir of the police station in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him there, during that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know a gentleman by the name of Stupar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell us who he is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: If you're referring to Milos Stupar, he was a member of the special police brigade, the Sekovici detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him there on that particular day, July 13th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him anywhere. I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But you knew him. If you saw him, you would know -- you would recognise him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, how long did you stay at that location? You told us that you got there sometime on the afternoon of July 12th. You were there on the 13th. How long were you at that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I was there in Sandici the whole time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But at what point or what day did you leave Sandici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: It was the second day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Before dusk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. That's the 13th then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us where you went, where you and the other men went.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Part of the unit had left previously to Bratunac. The members of the Bratunac station had gone to that young man's funeral, as did some other people who knew that family. And some had gone to Zvornik escorting the young men from Zvornik who had been wounded. It seems that they had first gone to Bratunac where they were given first aid, and then they were transported by car to Zvornik, to the hospital there. While the rest of the unit left the area in the evening. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us who gave you the orders to leave that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I think it was Dragomir Vasic. I don't remember exactly, but I think it was him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you recall what the orders were, what his exact orders were, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you could help us out here a little bit. You indicated that at -- initially when you were told to go to Bratunac, Mr. Vasic had directed the unit, the company, to go and report to Borovcanin. And so the company is under the subordination or resubordinated to Borovcanin. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- so at that point in time, I take it your commander is Borovcanin, your immediate commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please tell us: Where does Vasic fit in? What does he hit into this equation now, now that you have been resubordinated? Because it would appear, at least to some of us, that you might have two commanders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: It's hard to explain. Mr. Borovcanin at that time was the commander of all the police units there as a member of the special police brigade; while Mr. Vasic, as the chief of the centre, had other powers on the territory of the centre in which he was employed. I think at that time, my chief was Mr. Borovcanin; that's at least how I understood things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, then help us out here a little bit. If your chief was Mr. Borovcanin, then how could Vasic then give you an order to leave that location and go someplace else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Probably they had agreed among themselves, the two of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You don't know, in other words, the exact -- what transpired between those two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, I don't, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I went with those lads to Milici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, once you got there, did you receive any other orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Not that evening, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the next day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes. On the next day we were immediately called upon to go to Zvornik and to report to the centre. And there we would get new orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And when you say "the centre," that would be where Mr. Vasic is located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic also had a deputy, did he not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes. It was Mr. Mane Djuric at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall to whom you reported when you went to the centre in Zvornik, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I can't be precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I can't be precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it have been one of those two or could there have been somebody else as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I didn't ask you this question before, but the deputy of the centre, Mane Djuric, do you know whether you saw him in Bratunac or Potocari or on the road when you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I didn't see him at all during those days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us, if you recall, what orders you received from the centre, and this now would be, if our timing, if your recollection of the chronology is correct, this would be July 14, 1995. What orders did you receive from the centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: As far as I can remember the chronological order of things, we got an order that we should go off in the direction of Baljkovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is Baljkovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you precisely, but from Zvornik we were to go there to protect the line facing Tuzla. The army was holding it, because part of the forces -- they were mentioning the number of 15.000 who had crossed over to Crni Vrh and set out towards Baljkovica, so that they wouldn't come up from the back and attack those forces. My unit and several other units of the military police and the army - I don't know all the units that were there - were to prevent them attacking from behind, from the back of those people holding the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you go there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how long you were there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: We stayed there the whole night. The fighting went on all night and the following day until -- I don't know what time it was. And then some sort of agreement was reached, and those people passed through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were you at any point in time given any orders to participate in any executions of any prisoners that might have been taken in that area or from other areas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No. No. Nobody ever ordered me to do anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, once there was this agreement for some of those -- for part of the column or the column to go through towards Tuzla, what did you do? Did you stay there or were you given other orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I stayed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how many days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: One day -- that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we know that there was some heavy fighting there. Did you lose any men over there? Did the company lose any men over there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes. One was seriously wounded and one policeman was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it as we saw with the incident that happened on the early hours of the 13th of July, there would be records with respect to that death and that injury? There would be some records somewhere from a soldier of -- a member of a company losing his life and another one getting injured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, I want to show you a document what has been previously marked for identification purposes, though I don't believe it has been admitted into evidence, as P159.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And we have some extra copies, Your Honour, just one. Perhaps the Judges can share. We can put it on the ELMO, this document. I am told that the document was admitted, so I want to correct myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, have you seen this document before coming here today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did I show you this document last night when I met with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Last night, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But before last night, you did not see it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, no. Never before that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And last night did you have an opportunity to read the relevant portions with respect to the company that you were involved in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And at the last page of this document we see the name. It's uncertain whether that is the actual signature of the individual. But do you -- are you able to read that signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Ljubisa Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in this document with respect to the company that you were involved in, does this more or less accurately reflect the activities that you were engaged in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: For the most part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And in this document on the second page, it talks about the 2nd Company being sent to Srebrenica to form the public security station. Do you know whether that was actually ordered? Do you have any knowledge of that, of what the 2nd Company was doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I heard about that later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. All right. So you cannot vouch for what the 2nd Company was doing, but as far as the 1st Company, to your understanding --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I couldn't, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But with respect to the particular company that you were engaged in, it's your understanding that the activities listed here are more or less as they occurred, to your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I would have to read it, but yes, I think that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, I want to show you another document, what has been introduced into evidence as P386. And it should be P386B. We have A as in English, B as in B/C/S or Srpski. And we can put the English one on the ELMO. Now, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Only last night, never before last night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And from looking at this document, it would appear that it was generated by Mr. Kovac. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you know Mr. Kovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Only from television.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But did you know his position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: He was the Minister of the Interior at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course MUP falls under that ministry. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want you to look at the very last paragraph that's numbered 5. All right. And of course -- now, it -- under number 5 it says: "On arrival at his destination, the unit commander is obliged to make contact with the corps chief of staff, General Krstic." So --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we look at number 3, it states that the commander who was designated would be Ljubisa Borovcanin. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know from your observations or from any hearsay, perhaps from Mr. Borovcanin himself, whether Mr. Borovcanin made contact with General Krstic, and if so what, if anything, was talked among themselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't know what they talked about. I think Mr. Borovcanin was there in that headquarters, or whatever its name was, with those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you don't know what, if anything, the two discussed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Finally, I failed to ask you: What were the means of communications that you had available to you when you were out in the field during those days? What means of communications were available to you and --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Motorolas, G530.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. How many Motorolas were in the company, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Three or four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with that Motorola, with whom were you capable to communicate with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: The komandirs of the squads, I think, within the unit. I can't remember exactly, platoon komandirs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we're talking MUP now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did -- do you know whether you had any means of directly communicating with the Bratunac Brigade duty officer or the Bratunac Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever told that in the event you needed assistance or you needed clarification or that you needed some orders or any materiel needs to contact the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I understand your testimony correctly, to the best of your knowledge during that period from the moment that you went to Bratunac to the time that you left that area and went back and -- to where you had come from, you had no contact with any members of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I guess I have a couple more. Back to the communication. Could you communicate directly with Mr. Borovcanin through your Motorola?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't remember, but it's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about with Mr. Vasic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, no. Never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about with the Bratunac police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I think -- yes, I think we could. Not from every position, but I think we could, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much, sir. I have no further questions. Mr. Stojanovic may have some questions and the Prosecutor and perhaps the Judges will as well. I would appreciate it if you could be as frank and forthcoming in your answers to them as you were with me. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any questions to ask?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour, and good morning to the witness. Our Defence team has no questions for this witness in view of the testimony given here so far today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Issa, any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I do have some questions. Thank you. I'm just wondering if I can get the podium from Mr. Karnavas. Cross-examined by Ms. Issa:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. I'd like to start off with one of the last points. You indicated, sir, that Mr. Borovcanin, you saw him in with General Krstic at one point. And I believe what you said was that he was somewhere -- he was in that place with the -- with those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I object. It mischaracterises the evidence. I don't believe the gentleman ever said he saw Mr. Borovcanin with General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps that was my mistake, Your Honour. I'm just going to start over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, where did you see Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I saw Mr. Borovcanin on one occasion in Sandici. He passed by and stopped for a while and then left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you ever see Mr. Borovcanin in the Bratunac Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you mean when you said you "saw him with some people"? What people are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: You mean in Sandici?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you say that's the only place you saw him, so to whom --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: He was standing around with some people there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who are those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't know. Policemen I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, Mr. Karnavas earlier showed you a report that was prepared by Mr. Borovcanin which was Exhibit P159, which basically outlines the activities --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, what's the matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not sure it was actually prepared. That has not been fully established. It's signed by Mr. Borovcanin, but we don't know whether it was prepared by Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But you used it anyway?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I did. It might well have been generated by Mr. Borovcanin. There is a signature there. It hasn't been identified. I'm not saying that they cannot use it, but just to say that it was Mr. Borovcanin's work product, I don't know. Just a point of clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's a very, very minor issue since this document has been admitted into the evidence. I hope you could refrain from standing up on those trivial matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, did you yourself prepare a report outlining the activities of your unit during that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, I did not. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, as commander, wouldn't you have to or shouldn't you have prepared a report outlining your activities during that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No. It wasn't a regular police duty, this writing of reports. There were wartime activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, isn't writing reports normally a regular police duty, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes, when you're doing regular police work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're making the distinction between writing reports for regular police work versus combat activities. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Well, I didn't write any reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the 12th of July, sir, weren't you clearing minefields with members of the Bratunac Brigade on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No. The members of the Bratunac Brigade did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your company wasn't involved in that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: We were standing close by. It's right by the bridge, and that's where the separation line was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Didn't you tell us earlier, sir, that the report that was shown to you, signed by Mr. Borovcanin, was accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I didn't read it in detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well -- do you have a copy of that report with you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If not, I'm going to ask Mr. Usher to provide a copy to you. We can put the second page on the ELMO of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps we can look at the second page in the B/C/S version, sir, paragraph 2. Now, it's dated 12 July, and I'll just read part of it slowly. "Between 5.00 and 6.30 hours, the pioneers of the Bratunac Brigade, led by Captain Gavric cleared a passage through a minefield or groups of mines towards Budok [phoen] or immediately around the Zuti Most-Potocari road. Members of the 1st Company of the Zvornik special police unit led by a pioneer from the Bratunac Brigade set off through the cleared passages towards Potocari to create the conditions for the introduction of hardware." And then it goes on. And at the end of it, it says: "The first task to take control of the UN checkpoint on Zuti Most was completed successfully without any incidents." Do you see that there, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, what's the problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The problem is she's trying to discredit the witness by saying that his unit was clearing mines. He indicated that the Bratunac Brigade was clearing mines, that they were standing around. Now it's clear from what she read that it comports with his testimony. So I object to the means of trying to discredit the witness by misrepresenting what's in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You haven't heard the question yet. She just read certain portions of that document. I see no problem in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I have to say, Your Honour, I think Mr. Karnavas's comments are totally inappropriate, given the circumstances. And I would ask him to refrain from making comments of that nature in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, it appears from this paragraph that your unit was involved in clearing passages towards Potocari. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, it's not right. We had no activities going on in that part. All we were doing was standing around. We didn't have professionals for that kind of thing. It was engineers from the combat brigade, or I don't know who. They tried to remove the mines and I know that one man was killed. But we had no movement at all, no activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why would it say then here, sir, that "members of the 1st Company of the Zvornik special police unit led by a pioneer from the Bratunac Brigade set off through the cleared passages towards Potocari to create the conditions for the introduction of hardware?"

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is a mischaracterisation. It doesn't say that they cleared the passage.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It says they --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ms. Issa just read that paragraph. I don't think the reading has something wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, she's posing a question based on her interpretation of that passage. And furthermore --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, the question was why. I don't think that's an interpretation of the passage. I read the passage out as it is stated. And I would ask Mr. Karnavas, perhaps, let us get through this and object if there is a objectionable question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you look at her exact question, it mischaracterises what is on the paper to the question herself. What I am suggesting here is from reading this, it's very clear that they went through the cleared passage, not that they were clearing the passage. There is a big distinction. That's all I'm objecting to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Issa, just keep the first part. Why would it say it here. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, I think we know what we said at this point here, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you answer that question, sir: Why does that refer to the 1st Company of the Zvornik special police unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: May I be allowed to clarify?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: We were standing near Zuti Most, as it was called. That part of the minefield is 100 metres to the right. Now, I don't know what kind of hardware is mentioned or it was a wooded area. And somebody was killed there. This man was killed there, but there was no movement on the part of the police. And the man was taken away. He had been killed. And we waited for daylight. And we took the asphalt road and went after those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, sir, in order for you to go through that asphalt road after the passage was cleared, it says here that you were led or your unit was led by a pioneer from the Bratunac Brigade. Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you actually had to have some contact with at least that member of the Bratunac Brigade, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
