utterances.text: The man went in front of everybody else, him and two others, two others whom I didn't know. I didn't know either of them or all three of them. They tried to do away with the mines, but he was killed. That's as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you were at Zuti Most, sir, didn't you do any reconnaissance of the enemy on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, there were no lines up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any intelligence of anything going on in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, nothing. I just heard strong explosions somewhere over there, towards Srebrenica, detonations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make any effort to find out what was going on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, I didn't have anybody to ask. We heard it a long way off. It wasn't there near us, because there was the line of the army there. We were behind their backs lying down in a ditch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any army troops there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: You mean at Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, in the area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes, the line was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you said, sir, earlier that you saw Milos Stupar -- or you didn't see Milos Stupar, but you know of Milos Stupar. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't Milos Stupar the commander of the Sekovici detachment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't think he was at that time. I don't know what was going on in that special brigade, but he wasn't there at the time for sure -- at least not in that area. Now, whether he was replaced by the man that was nicknamed Oficir, I really can't say. But I didn't see him anywhere in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Borovcanin told the Office of the Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection. Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin is not going to come in here to testify because he is at large when he failed to turn himself in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You haven't heard the question yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But it's what Mr. Borovcanin told the OTP. I have no opportunity to cross-examine him who is now somewhere outside BiH. So there lies the problem, Your Honour. And I think this problem came up once before, and I believe it was with Mr. Butler.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, let's see what the question is, then we'll decide whether this question is allowed or not. You may proceed, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Borovcanin told the OTP investigators that Milos Stupar was the commander of the Sekovici detachment at that time. Do you have anything to say about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about that. I really didn't see him there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And it would be fair to say, sir, that if anyone would know, it would be Mr. Borovcanin, given that he was in charge of the activities during that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin was the commander of the entire police force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Borovcanin also said that he found -- he did see Mr. Stupar in the area at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, my same objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't have an opportunity to cross-examine Mr. Borovcanin. He failed to turn himself in when he was allowed by the Prosecutor to turn himself in in light of his position rather than have him arrested like he arrested Mr. Blagojevic and some of the others. So I'm now under the -- I'm unable to at any point to confront Mr. Borovcanin as to what he said. Now, I can vouch for the court that Mr. Stupar will be here tomorrow or the next day testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, the question is not whether you have the opportunity to cross-examine Mr. Borovcanin. The question is that your witness may or may not answer that question. Whatever he answers we will accept. That's very easy. And during the cross-examination, I believe that the party who is doing the cross-examination could use whatever documents and whatever information for the basis of their question. There is no doubt about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the problem with that is: They took a statement from someone who was about to be arrested. They let him go or the person jumped. It doesn't matter. What matters is we don't have an opportunity at this point in time to confront that individual with the statement that he gave to OTP. That's part of the problem. And now they're using this statement. We understand that hearsay comes in. But this is not just mere hearsay. This is a total inability of the Defence to cross-examine this individual, who is more than just a suspect. He is indicted as I understand or was about to be indicted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I apologise for getting up, but speculating on arrests of targets and whether they jumped or the Prosecution let people go is really inappropriate, especially in front of a witness. And I -- on this point, clearly the Trial Chamber has set the groundwork for what can be asked in cross-examination. And this has been the groundwork that both sides have been working under for the entire -- entirety of this trial. In fact, there are documents of people that are actually in evidence that we may never see. And those are -- that's our understanding of the rule that you have set down, that's why this question is asked. It's a little late in the day to be suggesting that the rule is otherwise. As long as the questioner has good faith belief in the question. We are not suggesting our questions are evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll just -- I'll bring -- I'll search for the portion of the transcript where McCloskey himself corrected Mr. Butler who stood up to try to use Borovcanin as a basis for one of his answers and was told not to do that. And if I'm wrong, I'll readily admit it. But my recollection is that this was brought to Mr. McCloskey's attention and he himself cautioned Mr. Butler not to mention anything he had learned from Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, it is not proper to argue those procedural matters in front of a witness. Here we just want to get the testimony gone through. I believe your witness could have the ability to answer that question, even if it's a hearsay question. You may proceed, Ms. Issa. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I just need to respond briefly to the Mr. Butler comment because it's such a different matter. And he is correct, at times with our expert witness I would ask him not to refer to specific matters, such as this. Because he was an expert, his opinion was something that we were relying on. It's completely different than asking a witness a question. And so it -- this is apples and oranges and I just wanted to point that out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, I've already said that this is a procedural matter. Procedural matters have nothing to do with the present witness. Ms. Issa, you may proceed with your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Borovcanin told the Office of the Prosecutor investigators that Milos Stupar was there and that he found you and Mr. Stupar and asked you not to move from that position. Do you have any comment to make about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: In Sandici, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't know what period that was, but yes, Ljubisa Borovcanin did come. I said I'd seen him, but I don't know what day that was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the point is, sir: That he also said that he saw Mr. Stupar there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am going to go into another area at this point. I don't know if you wish to take the break now or you would like me to continue for five more minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, since you are changing the subject and since there is tension between the parties, I think we should have a break. We will resume at 25 past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, the hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to move to the Sandici meadow on the 13th of July. Did you see members of the Bosnian Serb army in the Sandici meadow at that time, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes, I did, several.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were they doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Nothing, standing around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And when the men surrendered, what was the -- what were the soldiers doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Nothing. They were standing around and the people were sitting on the meadow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Weren't they, in fact, securing the people on the meadow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: The people were quiet. They were just sitting there quietly in the meadow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And weren't these soldiers in fact securing them while they were sitting there on the meadow, which might be part of the reason they were sitting quietly there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Probably that was their task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see the army abuse Muslims the any way, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see young boys separated from the men on Sandici meadow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see -- it wasn't -- you didn't hear the announcement that boys that were born in 1980 or after to come out from the group and were separated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't see any of the boys separated, removed, from the group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you had two children, two young boys, that you put on a bus? Isn't that what you told us about earlier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And didn't those young boys come from the group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the young boys come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: From the left-hand side. There was some high grass, long grass, so they came through that long grass and turned up that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they came towards Sandici. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: They came out on to the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And why did you take those boys and put them on a bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: They were small boys. I didn't know what to do with them. They didn't know where they were going, where their parents were. They didn't know anything. I asked them where their parents were. One of the little boys said: Maybe they're in the buses. He said he didn't know. They got lost in the woods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see any older men that were separated, did you? The men were left on Sandici meadow. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, there was no separation there, as far as I could see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the wounded men ask to go on the buses that were going to Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I wasn't near them. I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't see anything? You didn't see any of the separations? You didn't see what happened to the wounded men? You didn't see what happened to the boys?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Weren't the Muslims ordered at some point to lie down on their stomachs and -- facing the ground and to say: "Long live Serbia"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see that either?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see dead bodies in the meadow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see that either? Did you hear Mladic tell the Muslims that if they had surrendered earlier, that there wouldn't have been so many wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I heard him talking, but I don't remember what he said, his words and the details. I said what I had heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you only heard that other part that you told us about earlier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't remember the details. I heard him speaking to them. It might have gone on for some five minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't he also tell them that they would be taken to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us which direction did the buses come from that took the men to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I can't say exactly, because some came from Konjevic Polje. Coming back and going to Konjevic Polje there were a lot of comings and goings. I can't really say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't see where they came from and loaded up the men and subsequently went to Bratunac? You didn't see that direction that they came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who loaded up the men on to the buses that took them to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Those people over there who were standing at the top of a small hill or bend.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who are those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, were they army? Were they police? Who are they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I think there were a -- some of both.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Didn't you tell the OTP investigators, sir, that the soldiers and special police escorted the men to Bratunac? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Probably they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And they also escorted the men to Kravica, the soldiers and the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: They took them all off in that direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "they took them all off in that direction," it was the soldiers and the police that did that, that escorted the men in the direction of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Some of them went in the buses, and the others went on foot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they -- whether they went in the buses or on foot, they were escorted by the soldiers and the police. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, can you tell us, sir, when is it that you left the Sandici meadow on 13 July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: At dusk, towards evening. I don't remember the time, but thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there any Muslims left when you left in Sandici meadow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, that 16 people were left behind were actually killed by members of the Jahorina unit --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't know --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would like to know if she's going to be posing these sorts of questions, especially the one with the 16 people. She can tell the witness where she got this information, from whom and what is the basis for this information, that 16 were left behind at Sandici meadow and that they were then taken and executed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll hear the answer from the witness first. Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know anything about that. I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you see any UN white APC going up and down the road calling out for people to surrender that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was a tank and a Praga and other equipment on Sandici meadow that day. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did they belong to, sir, that equipment, the Praga, the tank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I couldn't say. They were there that evening when we arrived, but whether they were there on the next day I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How is it, sir, that the men went to -- or got to Sandici meadow? Can you answer that? How is it the men got to Sandici meadow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: They were coming out next to that big house and crossing the road and sitting down on that meadow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was directing them to come out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: They were standing there, policemen, soldiers, showing them the way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the policemen and the soldiers were directing the men to come out from the hill and assemble them on the Sandici meadow. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes, pointing to the place they were to go to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And who were the -- what units did the soldiers belong to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What units did the policemen belong to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: On one of the pictures that the investigator had, I saw quite a few policemen whom I didn't know. I also saw others I did know. There was some from the special brigade police. I don't know who the others were, also policemen. This was another company, and I don't know what sort of company it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the buses came from that ultimately picked up the men, where they were brought from, how they came to be there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question fully. Could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who organised the buses to be brought to the meadow to pick up the men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, you indicated that you learned about the shooting in Kravica of a particular -- of one officer and of the wounding of the man nicknamed "Officer" about a couple hours after the incident. Isn't that what you told us before in the examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, amidst this talk, did you hear that another gentleman was also wounded, Milomir Stanojevic, who was a member of the Red Berets of the Bratunac Brigade at Kravica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't know about that. This is the first time I've heard of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, sir, I want to clarify one point. When you went to Bratunac because you were telling us you wanted to check on one of your officers that was killed. Do you remember telling us that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where you went exactly when you went to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: First I went to the police station, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And why did you go to the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: To organise the funeral, to see about the funeral, the family, about where the body was to be kept, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And did you go anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you went to Bratunac, you just went to the police station in Bratunac. Right? Isn't that what you just said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Yes. I was at the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you see there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: There were many soldiers and policemen. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't recognise the soldiers at the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When you went to Bratunac, did you see any men there on buses in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Not in front of the police station, certainly not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, did you see them anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can just have the Court's indulgence for a moment. I have no further questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any re-direct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I do. I just have a couple of questions to clear up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Re-examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you were shown a document that was purportedly prepared by Mr. Borovcanin that is Exhibit P159. And you were specifically pointed to the word "led," that the unit was "led by a pioneer from the Bratunac Brigade." My question to you, sir, is: When you were there by the Zuti Most, were you resubordinated or re-resubordinated to the Bratunac Brigade pioneer group that was doing the demining?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you taking any orders from them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you part after the Bratunac Brigade when you were there? Were you part of the Bratunac Brigade when you were at the Zuti Most waiting there as they were clearing the mines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: No. I was part of the police force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, the -- there were some questions with respect to what happened in Sandici. Could you please tell us whether you spent any amount of time with the men that were surrendering and they were going across the road and sitting on the meadow.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I didn't go up to the meadow at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know who was in charge at the meadow of those -- you said that there were soldiers and police. Do you know who was the komandir, the person in charge, of that activity at the meadow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you look at -- again, you haven't been to the terrain. Hopefully -- I know the Defence will be requesting that the Trial Chamber go to the scene to visit. But just -- if you could tell us, describe a little bit where you're situated and where the meadow is located, so at least we could try to picture it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I was some 50 or 100 metres downhill from that house among my men. The meadow was behind me about 100 or 150 metres away up the slope.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And could you please tell me: Were all your men bunched together, or were you spread out? Where were the men located that were in --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Behind those fences, there's a canal. That's where they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Were they all bunched together or --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Aside from the fact that it's a very leading question, I think we're now going way beyond the confines of the cross-examination. I don't see how any of this arises out of cross-examination. I'm objecting to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If you have a question to this witness, put it directly to this witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm trying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Because this is the redirect examination. As a rule, all your questions should be within the scope of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am well aware of the rule, and I don't mean to be disputatious. However, if I point -- if I could point out, the Prosecutor was trying to elicit information to suggest at closing argument that this man is being less than candid, because how could he be situated there with the men nearby and not hear and see the events described --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It is improper for counsel to make these comments in front of the witness, and he knows that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe so. I ask you just to put your question directly to this witness if that question is within the scope of the cross-examination. That's very simple.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please describe to us where your men were located and where you were located in relation to the meadow, so at least we know whether you had the ability to hear and see what was suggested, what was going on, at that time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: I couldn't see any of that. I've just said. It was behind my back. There were moments when we couldn't raise our heads because of the shooting, we couldn't look up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when the children -- you were asked about the two children. Did you pluck out those two children from the meadow, or did you find them at another location?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, this question has been asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: He's quite clear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My last question is: When you went to Bratunac, did you take a drive around the town to see what was happening, or were you there on any particular business that led you to the police station?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I mean I think the witness has already answered the question. I don't think this arises out of the scope of the cross-examination --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, he answered the first question -- well, he answered the second part of the question but not the first one. I think the main issue is that whether this witness drove around in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: This question is allowed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you drive around Bratunac to see whether there were any men in buses anywhere else, since you didn't see any in front of the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Believe me, I didn't want to drive around town. I went to the home of the person who had been killed, and then I went to the police station. His family wanted him to be buried in his uniform. And we had to find a new uniform to dress his body in. I didn't drive around the town. I didn't feel like doing that at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Vassylenko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: You mentioned the fighting in Sandici on 13th July, 1995, and also that soldiers took part in the fighting. Whom were these soldiers subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP-102
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know. I don't know who they belonged to, whether the Zvornik Brigade or the Bratunac Brigade, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Hvala. I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of Judge's questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. At this stage, are there any documents to tender? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just D126, the sheet with the pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: D126 -- maybe I have it wrong. I'm sorry. D125. I'm sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I guess there's no objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. This document is admitted into the evidence under seal. Are there any documents on the part of the Prosecution that is to be tendered?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague today your evidence. The usher will show you out of the room. We wish you a pleasant journey back home. You may go now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, we still have about 45 minutes left for the morning session. Do you have another witness waiting outside?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't, regrettably, because the other witness came last night and I needed -- and he's the only -- he's the last witness for this week because of some technical problems with passports. Hopefully, that won't occur again, so I would anticipate that that gentleman will only take tomorrow, probably about the same amount of time regrettably. And I know it's eating into my time, we have one witness left. But having said that, it will allow us now that Ms. Tomanovic is back to finalise and fine-tune our revised amended 92 bis -- or 90 -- 65 ter motion, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We are expecting that filing because I found that the 65 ter filings you made have some --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We've already covered that, Your Honour. We've covered that, and I'm going to rectify that, that's why I asked Ms. Tomanovic to come back earlier so we can get that done as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: For the future witnesses, I hope we could hear the witnesses one after the other, so that the time at your disposal will be made the best use of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's my intention, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And at this stage, are there any matters from the Prosecution? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Just briefly on a housekeeping matter but of some significance. Mr. Karnavas has mentioned a couple of times about a site visit, and it's one of the areas where Mr. Karnavas and I share similar views. I have not had a chance to speak to Mr. Stojanovic about it. But if you would like, we can present to you our reasons for that or -- in writing or orally, or we can enter into discussions to see if we can get all three counsel on that. But if you might be interested, I think it's something that at least Mr. Karnavas and I both would support. As you can imagine, it takes a lot of logistics and planning and -- so this basically the sooner the better, if you are interested. And that can be begun.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Can I hear initially from Mr. Stojanovic their views on that very issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We have not discussed this topic about an on-site inspection, and I think we should first talk about whether this is to be a reconstruction or an on-the-spot investigation. As for our Defence, in view of the terrain this would require more than one day. Since the municipalities of Bratunac and Srebrenica and the events in Zvornik are more than 50 kilometres apart, there is a physical distance of some 50 to 70 kilometres. So it would require at least a few days. In principle, the position of our defendant and of this Defence team, Your Honours, may view the places where the executions took place and the physical disposition of the offices in the Zvornik Brigade headquarters, which we tried to represent through a model in order to show where the duty officer's place of work was and where the communications system was located and how these communications functioned. Over the next few days - and we can do this today - we will meet with the Prosecution and Mr. Blagojevic's Defence team in order to agree on this proposal. And as this is my native area, I will be pleased to play the host to Your Honours there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much. Well, since the parties raised this issue, I hope the parties will file something in writing and list the reasons to bring the Bench there for a site visit. Well, I think that's all for today. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
